newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr despite RBI purchases.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr despite RBI purchases.

text.p: The rupee firmed sharply on Monday and only central bank dollar purchases stopped it making bigger gains in a market flush with bullishness toward India following Finance Minister P.Chidambaram's investor-friendly budget, dealers said.
The rupee closed at at 35.825/835 per dollar, well up from Friday's close of 35.89/90.

Dealers said the rupee, which traded at a high of 35.815 and a low of 35.875 on Monday, was on an uptrend most of the day but the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dollar purchases stepped in to curb the advance.
"The rupee was on a one-way street today...upwards," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
He said RBI dollar purchases at 35.835 levels pushed the rupee down to 35.83/84 from its intra-day high, before it retraced to the closing levels.
"Actually the RBI did not hit the market in a big way," the dealer said. "They were enquiring for prices and mopping up whatever was offered."
Dealers said they expected the rupee to maintain its strength against the dollar on Tuesday.
"Further dollar supplies are expected tomorrow," said a dealer. "Given the present level of demand, unless the RBI buys dollars in a big way, the rupee could gain beyond 35.80."
Dealers said forward premia opened lower on the back of the rupee's appreciation in the spot market and ended at the same levels.
"Premia opened down and ended at the day's opening levels after brief volatility," said a dealer. "The rupee's gains in spot led to forward dollar sales by exporters and rates fell."
He said there was some booking of forward dollars by importers which led to premia hardening marginally but rates did not fluctuate much and ended at opening levels.
Spot-September dollars opened at 1.36/1.40 rupees against Friday's close of 1.47/1.50 and moved up briefly to 1.37/1.39 before closing at opening levels, dealers said.
The annualised premia for six-monmth dollars ended Monday at 6.59 percent against friday's close of 7.19 percent.
